gaps.title: Some graph on 6 vertices has a partial-function AND-count circuit with fewer gates than every biclique cover of its edges has bicliques
gaps.statement: ∃ (G : SimpleGraph (Fin 6)) (C : PEqualNP.AndCount.AndCountCircuit 6), C.WellFormed ∧ (∀ I : Finset (Fin 6), (∀ v ∈ I, ∀ w ∈ I, ¬ G.Adj v w) → (∀ u, u ∉ I → ∃ v ∈ I, G.Adj u v) → C.eval I = false ∧ ∀ u, u ∉ I → C.eval (insert u I) = true) ∧ ¬ (∃ (k : ℕ) (X Y : Fin k → Finset (Fin 6)), k ≤ C.size ∧ (∀ i : Fin k, ∀ a ∈ X i, ∀ b ∈ Y i, G.Adj a b) ∧ (∀ a b : Fin 6, G.Adj a b → ∃ i : Fin k, (a ∈ X i ∧ b ∈ Y i) ∨ (b ∈ X i ∧ a ∈ Y i)))
gaps.unlocks: Where the AND count first departs from the biclique cover number
gaps.context: SKETCH: no proof is expected here: propose a cut: by first gates up to symmetry, by a structural invariant, by cases. enumerate the 156 graphs on 6 vertices up to isomorphism, compute each biclique cover number by brute force over covers, and search AND-count circuits (each side an OR of vertices and earlier gates) with one gate fewer for the partial-function condition. The two rows are a pair; one is true. In-house: the count equals the biclique cover number on every graph up to 5 vertices and fails on a 7-vertex graph (computed, not checked). Data lane. No sorry, no new axiom.
